title: Negotiated spike handshake and tiered overage refund policy
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: Customers on Dedicated want predictable throughput SLAs but also the ability to handle short-lived spikes without manual capacity increases. Current surge pools provide capacity, but billing is opaque (flat overage charges) and there is no negotiated handshake for planned or announced spikes. This ticket designs a protocol plus billing flow that lets tenants request temporary negotiated boosts (a handshake), fallback to surge pools if unavailable, and receive tiered invoice adjustments/refunds when platform-initiated mitigations reduce cost responsibility.

Goal: Implement a negotiated spike handshake API, bookkeeping for temporary boost windows, and a tiered refund mechanism that credits customers when platform-side mitigations (e.g., preemptive routing to lower-cost variants, graceful degradation) materially reduced their actual cost exposure. The flow should integrate with autoscaling policy signals and fleet controls so boosts are safe and observable.
acceptance_criteria: API: /v1/dedicated/{tenant}/spike-handshake accepts proposed window, max QPS, and optional pre-announcement token and returns Accepted/Queued/Declined with reason
Accounting: Boost windows are recorded with unique IDs and retained for 90 days for audit; usage meter attributes boost_id and boost_tier
Billing: Billing pipeline applies tiered refund rules automatically for boost windows where platform mitigation reduced billable seconds by >= 20%
Autoscaling integration: Fleet autoscaler can annotate scale ops with boost_id; no boost can cause eviction of reserved capacity for P0/enterprise tenants
Observability: Console shows per-boost timeline, estimated avoided-cost, and final refund amount once billing run completes
E2E tests: Simulated burst + handshake + platform mitigation yields expected refund in billing sandbox
technical_notes: Handshake model: optimistic optimistic-ack model — tenant posts desired window + expected QPS; controller replies with token and provisional allocation or reason for decline (capacity, conflict, policy)
Boost tiers: tier-1 (announced >24h), tier-2 (short-term announce 1-24h), tier-3 (emergency, <1h). Refund rates scale with tier and platform mitigation percentage

Storage: Persist boost metadata in billing-qualified ledger table (append-only) with index on tenant_id and boost_id. Ledger rows include estimated_reserved_tokens, actual_billable_tokens, mitigation_delta_percentage
Policy: Admin operator can configure per-tenant boost caps and global surge pool soft-limits via fleet-control RBAC surface

Trade-offs: Stronger guarantees require pre-reserving capacity which increases cost. We prioritize negotiated boosts where tenants accept provisional allocation expiry semantics to avoid permanently carved capacity
Edge cases: overlapping boosts across tenants should be resolved using fair-share algorithm; if contention, lower-priority boosts receive queued response
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Implement handshake API behind feature flag; enable for internal tenants and two pilot customers; manual billing verification
Phase 2 (beta): Wire automated refund calculation in billing pipeline; expose boost timeline in Console; enable for invited tenants
Phase 3 (GA): Open to all Dedicated customers with UI for negotiated boosts and tenant-configurable policies
Operator playbook: runbook for declining/overriding boosts and communicating invoice adjustments to customer success
test_plan: Unit tests for handshake validation and policy decision matrix
Integration test: end-to-end surge from request -> allocation -> autoscaler annotation -> billing-run with mitigation credit
Chaos test: simulate fleet shortage and verify queued/declined responses and fair-share enforcement
Billing reconciliation test: validate ledger entries vs billing output in sandbox account
